samples_judged.question_text: What is the result of the fraction operation shown?
What is the result of the fraction operation shown?
A shape is divided into 4 equal parts. 3 parts are shaded and 1 more part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded in all: \(\frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{4}\)?
A shape is divided into 5 equal parts. 3 parts are shaded and 1 more part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded in all: \(\frac{3}{5} + \frac{1}{5}\)?
A shape is divided into 10 equal parts. 3 parts are shaded. If 1 shaded part is taken away, what fraction of the shape remains shaded: \(\frac{3}{10} - \frac{1}{10}\)?
A shape is divided into 10 equal parts. 3 parts are shaded and 1 more part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded in all: \(\frac{3}{10} + \frac{1}{10}\)?
A shape is divided into 10 equal parts. 1 part is shaded and 1 more part is shaded: \(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{10} = ___\)
Shade the shape to show the result of 5/6 - 1/6.
A shape is divided into 4 equal parts. 2 parts are shaded and 1 more part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded in all: \(\frac{2}{4} + \frac{1}{4}\)?
Shade the shape to show the result of 1/10 + 1/10.

verdicts.reasoning: These items involve fraction addition. Some use visual interaction payloads with 'operation': 'add' (like seed 127 with 1/10 + 1/10), while others use textual prompts explicitly showing addition (e.g., seed 42: '3/4 + 1/4').

These items focus on fraction subtraction. Seeds 11 and 23 use the FractionModel visual payload showing subtraction (e.g., '2/6 - 1/6' and '3/10 - 1/10'), and seed 103 tasks the student to shade the result of '5/6 - 1/6'.

All addition and subtraction problems use similar fractions, meaning the denominators are the same for both operands. Examples include 2/6 and 1/6 (seed 11), 3/10 and 1/10 (seed 23), and 3/4 and 1/4 (seed 42).

These specific seeds utilize interactive visual models to represent the fraction operation. Seeds 11 and 23 use a 'FractionModel' for reading, while seeds 103 and 127 use a 'FractionShade' payload requiring the student to interact with the model.
